original_test_intent: Validate the Error Type enumeration of every applicable SMBIOS Type 18 32-bit Memory Error Information record, its association with memory inventory/error context, and persistence or explainable lifecycle after reboot without creating a fault.
original_method: Collect complete raw and decoded Type 18 records plus related Type 16/17 and Type 33 context, preserve each handle and numeric Error Type, apply the approved current-versus-stale/no-record policy, and compare the same evidence after an approved reboot.
manual_activity: A user supplies the expected diagnostic-state policy and approves the reboot plan; no memory-fault injection, DIMM manipulation or manual observation is part of this case.
required_inputs: Applicable SMBIOS version and Type 18 Error Type enum policy
Expected no-record, Unknown, OK, stale and active-error semantics
Type 16/17/18/33 handle relationship and Type 33 applicability rules
Validated raw-capable parser plus read-only EDAC/kernel/BMC context
Approved reboot window and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and error-context collection; do not inject correctable or uncorrectable memory faults.
Do not clear diagnostic history merely to obtain a desired value.
Preserve raw handles and numeric values before interpretation; distinguish Type 18 history from live health.
Require reboot approval and recovery access; stop on invalid enum, dangling relationship or boot failure and do not auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete Type 16/17/18/33 and read-only error context, decode Error Type under the approved schema/freshness policy, and compare pre/post reboot.
Report absent, stale, invalid or changed records without assigning the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve Error Type/no-record/freshness expectations and reboot/recovery plan.
Resolve whether a diagnostic record represents acceptable history or a current failure and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The field name is correct, but grep -A1 loses the Type 18 handle, raw enum, companion fields and relationship/freshness evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive full raw and decoded Type 16/17/18/33 records; report each Type 18 handle, raw/normalized Error Type, linked context, record-freshness interpretation and pre/post diff.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Type 18 Error Type scope, linked script and 5/5-minute estimates are retained; no fault injection or unapproved history clearing is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse the complete Type 18 record set, retain numeric Error Type values and handles, correlate related SMBIOS/error context, apply the approved freshness policy, and repeat after reboot without stimulation.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Platforms exposing SMBIOS Type 18 records; Type 33 correlation applies where extended addresses are present.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, firmware, dmidecode/parser and OS error-subsystem versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 18 Error Type and Type 33 definitions plus the project diagnostic-record lifecycle policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces isolated label grep with full record identity, numeric enum, relationship and lifecycle interpretation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects invalid enums, dangling or ambiguous records and stale-history misclassification that text matching misses.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved enum, relationship and record-freshness expectations.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS error records may be historical or absent; this read-only case neither creates faults nor proves the error-reporting injection path.

project_override_considerations: A project may define acceptable no-record, OK, Unknown or retained-history states by platform, but must document them; an empty grep cannot be treated as PASS.
expected_evidence: Approved Error Type enum/no-record/freshness policy and platform identity
Complete pre-reboot raw Type 16/17/18/33 records with handles and SMBIOS version
Per-Type-18 numeric and normalized Error Type, related context and freshness decision
Read-only EDAC/kernel/BMC context preserved without history clearing
Approved reboot/health evidence and complete post-reboot semantic diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Error Type is a valid Type 18 field; missing expected state and freshness policy are project inputs, not contradictory source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Once policy and access are supplied, parsing and comparison are deterministic software work; reboot approval affects readiness, not capability.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds numeric enum, complete record identity, linked context and diagnostic-lifecycle semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains no-fault and recovery safeguards while restoring FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates execution readiness and engineer interpretation from automatable evidence collection.

review_improvement: Prevents a decoded label or missing grep result from passing without proving which error record, numeric state and lifecycle were evaluated.
independent_technical_reasoning: Type 18 enumeration, handle correlation and pre/post comparison are automatable read-only operations; the owner-defined meaning of retained diagnostic history does not introduce a manual core action.
